A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The player's downward check tests bits 0–1 at $0C57 and, for the next column, at $0C7A; the player's horizontal checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile. For entities, the downward scan at $450C tests bits 0–1 at $4532 and $4542, and the horizontal test at $460C reads four attributes through $4632 (at $464C), keeping bit 1 of the first two and bit 0 of the last two.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

Absolute jump whose target is stored in its operand before it runs: $B96C writes the low byte $B976 and $B972 the high byte $B977. The load holds $FF00 there.

Five low bytes of state targets, paired with the high bytes at $B97D: $B982, $B99F, $B9F1, $BA4C and $BA6D, the handlers for states 0 to 4. The dispatcher at $B966 reads them at $B969 with Y = state $1AB1,X, which the handler's own code keeps between 0 and 4.
Five high bytes of state targets, paired with the low bytes at $B978: $B982, $B99F, $B9F1, $BA4C and $BA6D. The dispatcher at $B966 reads them at $B96F with Y = state $1AB1,X.

Call the event helper. If it returns, call $3020 twice: store the first result masked with $0F in $1AC2,X and the second masked with $80 in $1AD3,X. Set $1AE4,X=4 and $1AB1,X=1, then fall through into state 1.
Call the event helper again. If it returns and $1AE4,X is nonzero, decrement it and return; otherwise continue at $B9AB. Thus a normally returning state-0 invocation leaves this byte at 3.

Decrement $1AC2,X. If nonnegative, call the frame helper at $BA7B, copy $1AD3,X to the working byte $BAE8, then call $45BC for a negative direction or $4574 otherwise with A=6. If the returned value masked with 6 is 2, return; otherwise continue at $B9D0, as when the countdown goes negative.

Reached when the countdown $1AC2,X goes negative ($B9AE) or when the state-1 move returns a value whose AND 6 is not 2 ($B9C7). Call $3020. If its result is nonnegative, select state 0. Otherwise call $3020 again, store its top bit in $1AD3,X, set $1AE4,X=4 and $1AF5,X=8, and select state 2.

Call the event helper at $BAA1. If it returns and $1AE4,X is nonzero, decrement it and return. Otherwise save $1AD3,X at $BAE8 and inspect $1AF5,X. A positive value is passed to $4342 and then decremented. Zero is replaced by $80. For zero or a negative value, call $44DE with its low seven bits in A (0 on that first pass) and select state 0 if it returns carry set; otherwise continue at $BA3A. The positive path and $BA3A both go on to the frame update at $BA10.
Call the frame helper at $BA7B, then call $45BC for a negative saved direction or $4574 otherwise with A=8. If carry is set, toggle bit 7 of $1AD3,X; otherwise return.
For a negative $1AF5,X below $8C, increment it. Values at least $8C stay unchanged. Both paths continue to the frame update.
Decrement $1B17,X. If nonnegative, load A=8 and tail-jump to $45BC when $BAE8 is negative, otherwise to $4574. If negative, toggle bit 7 of $1AD3,X, copy $1B28,X to $1AB1,X and return.
Decrement $1AC2,X and return if the result is nonnegative. If negative, call $4B0E with A=$50 and jump to $5DB9.

Copy $1AD3,X to $BAE8. Increment $1B06,X and reset it to zero if the result is at least 3. Double the resulting byte, add 6 if the saved direction is negative, then add $19E5,X and store the low byte in $19C3,X.

Copy $1AB1,X to $1B28,X and call $792C and $732A. If $732A returns carry set with positive $1A6D,X, call $72FC, rotate $BAE8 right through its carry into $1AD3,X, set $1B17,X=8 and $1AB1,X=3, discard one return address and return.
Carry set from $732A with zero or negative $1A6D,X sets $1A8F,X=$FF, $1AC2,X=10 and $1AB1,X=4, then discards one return address and returns.
When $732A returns carry clear, call $7227. Return if carry is clear; otherwise load A=4 and tail-jump to $5D7A.

Working direction byte, a copy of $1AD3,X: state 1 ($B9B6), state 2 ($BA00) and the frame helper ($BA7E) store that field here, and the event helper rotates the $72FC carry into it at $BAB9 and copies it back to $1AD3,X at $BABC. State 1 ($B9BB), the state-2 movement ($BA15), state 3 ($BA53) and the frame helper ($BA91) test its sign with BIT to choose the direction or the frame offset.

Load 19: one byte, $BB in the load, between the direction byte at $BAE8 and the handler at $BAEA. No instruction in load 19 reads, writes or indexes it; the resident title copy at $026C, whose index reaches it, runs only after $023D has loaded load 1 again.

If $1A7E,X is zero, increment it. A nonzero $1A8F,X selects the effect path at $BB69; otherwise call the event helper at $BB78. If it returns, decrement $1B28,X and set $19C3,X to $19E5,X plus 2 when the result is negative, otherwise to $19E5,X.

When the decremented timer $1B28,X equals $FC, spawn only if $1A29,X is nonzero: copy X to Y and call $190B, which returns a free slot in X with carry set, or carry clear with Y untouched. A failed call restores X from Y at $BB22 and a successful one at $BB61 after filling the new type-$2C slot, so whether the spawn is skipped, succeeds or fails, this entity’s $1B28,X is reset to 20 at $BB63 before returning.

On allocation carry set, initialize the returned X slot as type $2C, copy $193B/$197F/$194C/$1990 from slot Y, set $19E5/$19C3 to $19E5,Y plus 6, clear $1AA0, copy $4DAE to $1AC2 and store $49 shifted right in $1AD3. Restore X from Y.
Set $19C3,X to $19E5,X plus 4 and $1B28,X to 5, then return.
Call $792C and $732A. Carry clear calls $7227 and may call $5D7A with A=4. Carry set returns when $1A6D,X is positive; otherwise call $4B0E with A=$40, load A=4 and jump to $5DB9.
When $1B28,X is zero, branch to $BBE0. Otherwise set $19C3,X to $19E5,X plus the old $1B17,X, set $1A07,X=1, toggle $1B17,X between zero and 2, and call $35C1 with $1B28,X in A.

If $1A29,X is zero, jump to $4454. Otherwise call $792C and $1179; carry set jumps to $4454. If carry is clear, call $7227: carry clear returns, while carry set calls $5D7A with A=4 and then jumps to $4454.

Copy $1AC2,X/$1AD3,X to $35BD/$35BE. If $1A29,X is zero, return. Otherwise use that display slot as Y to fill $35C0 from $4CCF,Y shifted right and $35BF from $4C4F,Y and $4C6F,Y combined by LSR/ROR. Call $34EA, OR its result with $A0, store it in $1B28,X and tail-jump to $35C1.

High bytes paired with the low-byte state target table at $BC22.

Call the input sampler at $3C4C and test $70, then $73, then $74 for zero, in that priority order. The sampler reads joystick port 2 active-low, so $70 is zero while fire is pressed, $73 while the stick is pushed left and $74 while it is pushed right.
If cursor mode $BE8E is negative, leave it unchanged; otherwise decrement it. Both paths enter the input-release wait at $BD9A.
If cursor mode $BE8E equals 1, leave it unchanged; otherwise increment it. Both paths enter the input-release wait at $BD9A.
Update the cursor colours through $BE61 and call $BDA5. While it returns carry set, repeat; on carry clear return to the cursor and poll loop at $BD62.

Call the input sampler at $3C4C; return carry set if any of $73, $74 or $70 is zero, that is while the stick is pushed left or right or fire is pressed (joystick port 2, active low), otherwise return carry clear.

Call the message routine with A, X and Y cleared. Patch the immediate comparison at $BDD6 with bit 0 of $9A4B. A negative cursor mode goes to $BE38. Entity index kept across the message calls: state 1 ($BC49) and state 2 ($BCDC) store X here, and state 1 at $BC5A, the finish at $BDE5 and the wrong-answer path at $BE3F reload it.

Set entity X-coordinate bytes $195D,X and $196E,X to $28 and $00, then return.
Set entity X-coordinate bytes $195D,X and $196E,X to $0A and $01, then return.
